reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker or PD data reported to confirm NK1 receptor engagement by fosaprepitant. However, fosaprepitant is a well-established NK1 receptor antagonist with known pharmacology, so target engagement is likely but not confirmed in this trial. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers reported to assess whether NK1 receptor antagonism affected downstream tachykinin signaling. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint (complete response - no vomiting) was not met. Only 1/11 patients (9.1%) in the fosaprepitant arm achieved complete response vs 0/9 (0%) in placebo arm. This represents a numerical improvement but the trial was underpowered to detect significance. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. The population was patients receiving high-dose IL-2 for metastatic melanoma/RCC, which may have unique nausea/vomiting mechanisms compared to standard chemotherapy. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Major confounder is the severely underpowered design with only 13 total patients (11 treatment, 9 placebo). The trial noted 'enrollment issues' suggesting difficulty recruiting patients. The small sample size makes any statistical inference unreliable.

failure_modes.evidence: Only 13 total patients enrolled (11 fosaprepitant, 9 placebo) with investigator commentary noting 'enrollment issues'. This sample size is far too small to detect meaningful differences in complete response rates.
